title: Getting started with psgc
text: Philippine Standard Geographic Code (PSGC) official list every geographic area Philippines — broadest (regions) granular (barangays). published maintained Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA). area identified unique 10-digit code geographic level: PSA releases updated PSGC files several times year new cities chartered, barangays created, codes renumbered. package bundles 12 releases Q1 2023 Q1 2026.

title: Getting started with psgc
text: default, every function package uses latest release. can always pass specific release name work older data.

title: Getting started with psgc
text: PSA occasionally renumbers abolishes areas releases. map_psgc() traces code forward later release can keep longitudinal datasets consistent. mapping_type column tells happened code: especially useful joining PSGC-coded survey data different years — use map_psgc() first normalise codes single release merging.
code: map_psgc("0100000000")  # forward to the latest release #>     old_code   new_code mapping_type from_release to_release #> 1 0100000000 0100000000       direct      Q1_2023    Q2_2026 map_psgc("0100000000", to = "Q4_2023") #>     old_code   new_code mapping_type from_release to_release #> 1 0100000000 0100000000       direct      Q1_2023    Q4_2023

title: Philippine Standard Geographic Code
text: psgc provides access Philippine Standard Geographic Code (PSGC) — official classification system geographic areas Philippines published Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA). bundles 12 releases (Q1 2023 – Q1 2026) exposes small, consistent set functions.

title: Philippine Standard Geographic Code
code: # Install from CRAN install.packages("psgc")  # Or install the development version from GitHub # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("yng-me/psgc")

title: Philippine Standard Geographic Code
text: Every function defaults latest release. Pass release argument work older data.

code: library(psgc)  # All geographic areas in the latest release ph <- get_psgc() nrow(ph) #> [1] 42046  head(ph) #>    psgc_code                     area_name geographic_level #> 1 0100000000       Region I - Ilocos Region              Reg #> 2 0102800000               Ilocos Norte              Prov #> ...

title: Philippine Standard Geographic Code
text: Plain English aliases accepted — need memorise codes:
code: get_psgc(geographic_level = "Region") get_psgc(geographic_level = "Province") get_psgc(geographic_level = "Barangay")  # Cities and municipalities together get_psgc(geographic_level = "city_mun")  # Multiple levels at once get_psgc(geographic_level = c("City", "Municipality"))

code: psgc_info("0100000000")           # Region I psgc_info(c("0100000000", "0102800000"))  # batch lookup  # Short codes are accepted — trailing zeros are added automatically psgc_info("01")      # → "0100000000" (Region I) psgc_info("01028")   # → "0102800000" (Ilocos Norte)

title: Get population data for a specific release — get_population
text: release release name [list_releases()]. Defaults [latest_release()]. details Logical. `TRUE`, adds `area_name` `geographic_level` columns PSGC release data. Defaults `FALSE`. geographic_level character vector geographic levels filter . Accepts canonical codes aliases [get_psgc()] (e.g. `"Reg"`, `"Region"`, `"Prov"`, `"city_mun"`, `"Barangay"`, etc.). `NULL` (default) returns levels. Implies `details = TRUE` internally resolve filter; column included result `details = TRUE` also requested. wide Logical. `TRUE`, pivots census years columns named `population_<year>` (e.g. `population_2015`, `population_2020`, `population_2024`), yielding one row per PSGC code. Defaults `FALSE`.

title: Get population data for a specific release — get_population
text: data frame. long format (default): columns `psgc_code`,   `population`, `year`, plus optionally `area_name` `geographic_level`.   wide format: columns `psgc_code`, `population_<year>` per census year,   plus optionally `area_name` `geographic_level`.

Accepts canonical codes (`"Reg"`, `"Prov"`, `"City"`, `"Mun"`, `"SubMun"`, `"Bgy"`) well common aliases `"Region"`, `"Province"`, `"Municipality"`, `"Barangay"`, `"Sub-Municipality"`, etc. Use `"city_mun"` (aliases like `"City-Municipality"`) include cities municipalities. `NULL` (default) returns levels. include_population_data Logical. `TRUE`, census population figures joined onto result, adding `population` (integer) `year` columns. geographic unit produces one row per available census year. Defaults `FALSE`.

Highly Urbanised Cities (HUCs) Independent Component Cities (ICCs) included pseudo-province entries barangays `province` value. title: Get PSGC data in wide (denormalised) format — get_psgc_wide
text: data frame one row per barangay following columns,   order: `area_code` 10-digit PSGC code barangay. `region_code` 10-digit PSGC code region. `province_code` 10-digit PSGC code province (      HUC/ICC acting province). `city_mun_code` 10-digit PSGC code city, municipality,       sub-municipality. `NA` barangays sit directly HUC       intervening city/municipality layer. `region` Region name. `province` Province name (HUC/ICC name province-free       cities). `NA` areas province layer (e.g. Pateros NCR,       City Isabela, Special Geographic Areas). `city_mun` City / municipality / sub-municipality name. `NA`       HUC barangays. `barangay` Barangay name. `urban_rural` Urban/rural classification barangay. `island_region` Island group barangay.

title: psgc 0.1.1
text: island_region values now consistently abbreviated ("L", "V", "M") across releases. Three older releases (Q4_2023, April_2024, Q2_2024) full spellings (“Luzon”, “Visayas”, “Mindanao”) now recoded data build step.

title: psgc 0.1.1
text: get_psgc_wide() returns denormalised wide-format data frame one row per barangay four geographic levels (region, province, city/municipality, barangay) spread columns. HUC/ICC barangays city_mun / city_mun_code set NA; areas province layer (e.g. Pateros, City Isabela, Special Geographic Areas) province / province_code set NA (#get_psgc_wide). map_psgc() gains changes_only argument. TRUE, rows code actually changed (mapping type "direct") returned, making easy identify renumbered abolished codes across releases.

title: psgc 0.1.1
text: map_psgc() rewritten fully vectorised algorithm. crosswalk pre-split hop per call codes processed simultaneously hop using match(), replacing previous per-code loop. yields roughly 500× speed-large code vectors (e.g. 1 000 codes: 94 s → < 0.2 s).
